Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not perform the task.", "input": "please turn this into a short, friendly email to Elena Park about booking guitar lessons. i'm an adult beginner and would like to start with one 45-minute lesson, ideally next week. i can do monday after 6 p.m. or saturday before noon, but i'm away this coming saturday, so don't offer that day; monday next week is possible. i'm not sure whether she teaches in person or online, so ask which format she offers rather than assuming. her profile has this exact line: “I teach adult beginners and can lend a guitar for the first lesson.” I'd like to ask whether I could borrow a guitar for that first lesson, and also ask what she charges. don't suggest times other than the ones i gave, and don't make it sound like anything is booked already. Keep the email warm and concise but not overly formal. i haven't decided if i'll continue after the first lesson, so don't imply that i'm signing up for a series. mention that i'm contacting her about lessons, not a performance or group class.", "output": "Write a short, friendly email to Elena Park asking about booking one 45-minute guitar lesson. The sender is an adult beginner and would ideally like to meet next week. They are available Monday after 6 p.m.; they can usually do Saturday before noon, but will be away this coming Saturday. Ask which format Elena offers—in person or online—and what she charges. Ask whether a guitar could be borrowed for the first lesson, based on this exact profile line: “I teach adult beginners and can lend a guitar for the first lesson.”\n\nDo not suggest any times beyond those given or imply that a lesson is already booked. Keep the email concise and warm, but not overly formal. Do not imply the sender is signing up for a series; they have not decided whether to continue after the first lesson. Make clear they are asking about lessons, not a performance or group class."}]
